subject: ventures/pairwise-ranking
professional: a senior applied statistician who fits paired-comparison models (BradleyTerry2 / choix user, sports-ratings analyst); first checks: do the Bradley-Terry and Davidson strengths, standard errors, home factor and tie parameter match an independent fit of the same likelihood; is the home-advantage LR p-value the chi-square(1) tail; is the Ford existence check right in every tie mode; are rank ranges and P(ahead) consistent with the fitted covariance; does the input reader misread a CSV.

evidence.correctness: Independent pure-stdlib Python (/tmp/claude-0/audit-pairwise-ranking/indep.py, does not import or read engine.mjs): Davidson's likelihood written in pi form with the README's home factor, maximised by damped Newton on finite-difference derivatives, SEs from the inverse FD Hessian then centred. Against `node cli.mjs data/premier-league-2023-24.csv --json --draws 0`: all 20 ratings within 0.05 points (my rounding), rating SEs within 0.005, alpha 0.504179 (se 0.142928) both, nu 0.729400 both, loglik -335.48137 both, home LR 12.938207 and p = erfc(sqrt(LR/2)) = 0.000322 both. Arsenal (home) v Liverpool 52.56/25.03/22.41% vs CLI 52.6/25.0/22.4. Zermelo/Hunter fixed point on the decisive games agrees with my Newton to 1.6e-9. Coffee data (plain BT, counts): ratings within 0.04, SEs within 0.005. Points from the PL CSV: City 91, Arsenal 89, Liverpool 82 (the published table, as data/SOURCE.md says). Independent MC (/tmp/claude-0/audit-pairwise-ranking/mc.py, Python Mersenne Twister, own Cholesky, 40,000 draws): P(City ahead of Arsenal) 0.63983 vs engine 0.63983; pTop City 0.577 vs engine 0.576 at 20,000 draws; 95% rank ranges 1-3, 1-4, 1-5, 18-20 identical. Defects are in input handling and one tie mode, not the fitted numbers: a header without a recognised word is read as a game (phantom players), and ties=half made every game two-way in Ford's graph.
evidence.completeness: README features walked: browser page (static, not loaded in a browser here; served-copy.mjs shows no placeholder origins), CLI text/--csv/--json/--predict (ran, all work), agent call `node platform/agents/tools.mjs call pairwise-ranking analyze` (ran, returns the summary), exported fit/fitMM/predict/readGames/strongComponents (used by the tests), three input shapes plus count column, semicolon and tab (engine tests pass), Davidson/half/drop ties, home LR test, Ford warning with a prior, runaway prior for home/tie terms (ran each). No TODOs or stubs. Gap: at the documented 2,000-player limit the fit is dense O(n^3) on the main thread (500 players 3.7 s; 2,000 players 147 s in Node).
evidence.verification: `node --test engine.test.mjs cli.test.mjs page.test.mjs usage.test.mjs`: 38 pass, 0 fail, 0.7 s. The core test reproduces 30 statsmodels-GLM / scipy-BFGS reference fits (eval/reference.json) to 1e-7..2e-5, plus property tests (score equations, invariances, count column). 6 mutants via quality_mutate.py: tie utility /2->/3, LR p-value lr/2->lr, runaway threshold 12->40 and centring 1/n->0 caught; P(ahead) variance -2cov->+2cov (engine.mjs:628) and rank-range upper quantile off by one (engine.mjs:602) SURVIVED, because the PL test only bounds aheadTopTwo in (0.6,0.7) and rank ranges by +-1. The half-mode Ford bug (engine.mjs:523) had no test.
evidence.craft: Read engine.mjs (710 lines), cli.mjs, engine.test.mjs, eval/make_reference.py. Clean pure functions, softmax parametrisation with sparse design rows, step-halving Newton, iterative Tarjan, CSV formula-injection guard. Defects: header detection clause `!first.every((c, k) => k > 1 && isNum(c))` is always true (k=0 fails) so it is dead (engine.mjs:191); dense n x n Hessian, Cholesky, inverse and a triple-loop covariance transform for up to 2,000 players on the UI thread; long one-line expressions in analyze(); the strongComponents comment trails off ('...see dominance', no such function, engine.mjs:251).
evidence.claims: Checked: 30 independent fits (pass, reference.json has 30 cases and the test reproduces them); MM vs Newton 1e-9 (pass, my MM 1.6e-9); Newton 4 to 8 iterations on the examples (pass, observed 4-6); tests about 2 s (pass, 0.7 s); page's PL numbers 64% ahead, ~59% top, home factor, 27% equal-tie (pass vs my recompute); data provenance and 91/89/82 (pass); 'the tool says which players cause it' (partial: with ties=half it gave the generic runaway warning without naming the unbeaten player); 'Up to 2,000 players' (partial: input cap, but see timing); disclaimer, privacy and limits present on page and README (pass, page.test.mjs).
evidence.fitness: Job walked: a league organiser pastes a season CSV (home,away,scores) and wants a ranking with uncertainty and home advantage; a sensory panel pastes preferred,other,count. Both run end to end from the CLI with sensible summaries and warnings. A user with headers such as 'Team A,Team B' or 'Winning team,Losing team' silently gets those header words as two phantom players plus a disconnected-groups warning and a prior; they would have to rename columns. No covariates, time decay or random effects (stated in Limits). Usable for its stated scope.
evidence.domain: Compared with Bradley & Terry 1952, Davidson 1970, Davidson & Beaver 1977, Hunter 2004 and BradleyTerry2 practice: MLE by Newton, observed-information SEs, centring with transformed covariance, LR test with chi-square(1) tail, Ford/Hunter existence via strongly connected components, penalised fallback, simulation rank ranges are all standard. Disclosed departure: home factor inside the tie term (keeps concavity). Undisclosed nuances a statistician would flag: 'the chance X is really stronger' is Phi(diff/sd), a flat-prior posterior reading of a frequentist estimate; the LR test after a penalised fit is not chi-square; the half-ties mode drew Ford's graph wrong (now one-way per decisive game).

defects.what: A header row with no recognised keyword (e.g. 'Team A,Team B', 'Winning team,Losing team') is read as a game: the header words become two phantom players, the fit gets a disconnected-groups warning and a prior, although the README and page say a header row is expected

With ties counted as half a win, every game (decisive ones too) was added both ways to Ford's graph, so the existence check always passed; an unbeaten player was caught only by the runaway check, with a generic warning that does not name the player (the page promises it does) and, with home on, a prior on the home term too
Two seeded mutants survive: flipping the sign of the covariance term in P(ahead) and an off-by-one in the rank-range upper quantile; the only checks are a (0.6, 0.7) band and +-1 rank bounds

Dense O(n^3) Newton, Cholesky, inverse and covariance transform on the browser main thread at the advertised 2,000-player limit: 500 players 3.7 s, 2,000 players 147 s in Node, so the page freezes for minutes at its stated cap
Header-detection clause `!first.every((c, k) => k > 1 && isNum(c))` is always true (fails at k=0), dead logic
'The chance X is really the stronger' is Phi(diff/sd), a flat-prior posterior reading, and the home LR test is reported as chi-square even after a penalised (prior) fit; neither nuance is stated

verdict: Every fitted number I recomputed reproduces: an independent pure-Python Davidson likelihood fit matches all 20 Premier League ratings, SEs, the home factor, nu, the log-likelihood and the home LR p-value; an independent MM fit matches the decisive and coffee fits; an independent Monte Carlo matches P(City ahead) 0.640, P(top) and every checked rank range. The reference suite against statsmodels and scipy is strong and 4 of 6 seeded mutants were caught. It meets the bar at 3 throughout, not above: a header without a recognised word becomes two phantom players, ties-as-half drew Ford's graph wrong so the 'says which players cause it' promise failed in that mode (fixed in the working tree with a test, score unchanged), the P(ahead) and rank-range quantile code is only loosely pinned, and the dense solver takes 147 s at the advertised 2,000-player cap. Versus BradleyTerry2 it lacks covariates and random effects, as its Limits say.
